results.query: How was SCAR-Net built and validated for distinguishing postoperative breast scars from recurrent lesions, and how much did it change radiologist performance?
results.answer: Using 34,376 ultrasound images from 5,710 patients across four hospitals, we developed a model incorporating scar-recurrence feature enhancer and boundary-sensitive attention network modules [PMID:42023157]. In multicenter validation, SCAR-Net significantly improved radiologists' diagnostic performance [PMID:42023157]. SCAR-Net increased AUC from 0.810-0.824 to 0.939-0.942, sensitivity from 0.775-0.782 to 0.934-0.941, and specificity from 0.839-0.872 to 0.935-0.950 (all p < 0.001) [PMID:42023157].

results.query: How did AI assistance change diagnostic performance in the simulated prostate-MRI triage workflow and in multicenter breast-ultrasound scar-versus-recurrence assessment?
results.answer: Among the 400 patients (median age, 66 years; IQR, 60-69 years) included for testing, radiologists achieved a sensitivity of 89.4% (95% CI: 85.8, 93.1) and specificity of 57.7% (95% CI: 52.3, 63.1) [PMID:41960994]. The AI system triaged and diagnosed 195 of 400 (49%; 95% CI: 173, 216) examinations with sensitivity of 94.7% (95% CI: 89.5, 99.9) and specificity of 94.7% (95% CI: 90.5, 98.9) [PMID:41960994]. The study reports: "MRI examinations of 500 men with suspected csPCa from four European centers were included." [PMID:41960994]. MRI examinations of 500 men with suspected csPCa from four European centers were included.

AI-triaging thresholds were calibrated on 100 examinations.

Reference standards were histopathology and/or 3 or more years of follow-up.

results.query: How did the fMRI acceleration method and the MR anisotropic-diffusion filters address different image-reconstruction problems, and what validation result did each report?
results.answer: Traditional MRI methodologies require full k-space information, which follows a unique data acquisition sequence to reconstruct the complete image, presenting a time-consuming obstacle for medical imaging techniques. Our study proposes a novel image reconstruction method to enhance the efficiency of data acquisition while maintaining high accuracy in activation detection [PMID:41951145]. By applying our approach to both simulated and experimental fMRI data, we successfully reduced total scan time while achieving a higher signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) in regions of interest (ROI). Compared with conventional reconstruction strategies, the proposed method demonstrates potential improvements in activation detection under specific acceleration and encoding conditions, while also providing voxel-wise estimates through a Bayesian framework [PMID:41951145]. The retrieved evidence does not establish: Problem addressed by the MR anisotropic-diffusion filters. The retrieved evidence does not establish: Validation result reported for the MR anisotropic-diffusion filters.

results.query: What association did the hemodialysis study find between AV-access flow and LV mass, and why can it not establish that lowering access flow will improve cardiac outcomes?
results.answer: In a multicenter cross-sectional study including a total of 241 patients, higher AV-access flow (FV) was significantly associated with increased left ventricular mass index (LVMI) with a mean difference of 22.83 (95% CI: 0.37 to 45.29; p = 0.046), whereas dialysis vintage was not (mean difference = 0.51; 95% CI: -0.41 to 1.45; p = 0.27) [PMID:41644509]. The study cannot establish that lowering access flow will improve cardiac outcomes because it was a multicenter cross-sectional study [PMID:41644509].
